trials.label: r1c2
trials.name: Footprint-pooled placement head
trials.hypothesis: A 1x1 stem reads each column's layer stack, two 3x3 convs (width 48), then for each brick type the max, min and mean of features over its footprint feed a per-type 1x1 head. Same recipe as proposal 1, r about 1.0. A placement is valid only if all its cells agree at the landing layer; footprint max and min act as any/all tests. Refuted if it does no better than proposal 1.

"""Column stem + 3x3 conv body + per-brick-type footprint-pooled placement head."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 64, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 4, "lr": 0.001}

STEM = 64
WIDTH = 48


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1)
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(STEM, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 1)
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * WIDTH, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = F.relu(self.stem(obs))
        f = F.relu(self.c1(f))
        f = F.relu(self.c2(f))
        h = F.relu(self.proj(f))
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.fps, self.type_heads):
            hp = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.name: Learned footprint-conv head
trials.hypothesis: Same body and recipe as r1c2 (1x1 column stem, two 3x3 convs). The fixed max/min/mean footprint pooling is replaced by a learned conv for each brick type, with kernel equal to its footprint (dy,dx), 32 hidden units, ReLU and a 1x1 logit. """Column stem + 3x3 conv body + per-brick-type learned footprint-shaped conv placement head."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 64, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 4, "lr": 0.001}

STEM = 64
WIDTH = 48
HEAD = 32


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1)
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(STEM, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.fp_convs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HEAD, (dy, dx)) for (dy, dx) in self.fps])
        self.fp_out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HEAD, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = F.relu(self.stem(obs))
        f = F.relu(self.c1(f))
        f = F.relu(self.c2(f))
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), conv, out in zip(self.fps, self.fp_convs, self.fp_out):
            fp = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            outs.append(out(F.relu(conv(fp))))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

"""Two-layer column MLP stem + 3x3 conv body, stem skip into footprint-pooled placement head."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 64, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 4, "lr": 0.001}

STEM = 64
WIDTH = 48


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.stem1 = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1)
        self.stem2 = nn.Conv2d(STEM, STEM, 1)
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(STEM, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + STEM, WIDTH, 1)
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * WIDTH, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = F.relu(self.stem1(obs))
        s = F.relu(self.stem2(s))
        f = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(self.c2(f))
        h = F.relu(self.proj(torch.cat([f, s], dim=1)))
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), head in zip(self.fps, self.type_heads):
            hp = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: No trials yet and scores stay hidden, so every trial is a blind best guess; only failures will be visible. The main constraint is the budget: the default recipe gets 32,768 steps, which is just 8 updates of 4,096 samples with the learning rate decaying to 0. Making more, smaller updates at the same compute is probably the biggest lever. Training cost is charged per sample and a cheaper network still costs the same (r<1 counts as 1), so the networks should stay at about the starting cost. On task structure: a placement is right only if every footprint cell is consistent at the layer where the brick lands. Max, min and mean pooling over each brick's footprint after learned layers is allowed and gives an any/all-style test that a 1x1 head must otherwise learn. Proposal 1 is a recipe-only control; proposal 2 adds the footprint head on the same recipe.
analyses.2: No scores are shown, so I can only reason about design. Both round-1 trials trained without errors. Each kept the 32,768-step budget at r≈1 and used 4× more updates (64 envs × 16 steps). Whether a brick placement is right depends mostly on local information. The agent needs the column heights under the footprint (the landing layer is their maximum) and whether the target has cells at that layer across the whole footprint. The order of placements only matters locally, under overhangs. The deciding operation is therefore an "all cells agree" test across the footprint, which max/min/mean pooling only approximates. A learned convolution shaped like each brick's footprint can combine the footprint cells nonlinearly at little cost. The two trials left need to differ: one changes the architecture (learned footprint head), the other tests a sharper training recipe on the r1c2 network.
analyses.3: I can't see any scores, so I can only reason about likely effects. All four trials trained without errors and stayed well inside the compute and time limits, so footprint-shaped heads are safe to use. Two things probably limit this task most. First, the sample budget is tiny: about 30,000 steps for an action space of about 400. Second, the network must reason about each column: the layer a brick will land on has to match the target's layers in every cell of the footprint. Two concrete changes target these. One is a recipe-only change to the r1c2 network: fewer PPO epochs buy about 1.9 times as many fresh samples and updates for the same compute. The other is an architecture change to r1c2: a deeper per-column stem plus a skip connection, so exact per-cell information about the column reaches the footprint head without being blurred by the 3x3 convs. Each changes one main thing relative to r1c2. Because 2-seed results are noisy, the final selection depends on the real dev scores.
